svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Inter, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: Where the bytes go
One decode step: 8B model, BF16, 4K context, batch size 1. Everything the GPU must move to produce one token.
model weights
16 GB
KV cache: 0.54 GB at 4K context — but 4.3 GB at 32K
Total: 16.6 GB moved per token, at ~3.35 TB/s → a 4.9 ms floor before any arithmetic happens.
Note what is not the bottleneck: attention.
Attention is compute-bound at decode. The starvation is weight reloading — which is why so many optimizations target the blue bar.
Every optimization in this series attacks one of these
Shrink the bytes
quantization (W10–11) · GQA and MLA (W13) · sliding window and SSMs (W13, W19)
Move fewer of them twice
FlashAttention keeps attention intermediates out of memory entirely (W12)
Pack them better
PagedAttention — same bytes, far less waste, so more users fit (W6)
Amortize the load
continuous batching across users (W5) · speculative decoding across tokens (W16)
Split the workload
disaggregated prefill/decode — the two regimes get different GPUs (W17)
Keep this picture. Every week from here is one of these five moves, and we will come back to this bar to say which.
